question: Why were some of the rarest wombats moved to a second refuge in southern Queensland from 2009?
answer: So that one disaster could not end the species. Every northern hairy-nosed wombat lived at Epping Forest, where a single fire, flood or outbreak could wipe them out. From July 2009, 15 were moved in several transfers to Richard Underwood Nature Refuge near St George; the first joey there was confirmed in 2011.
move: Keep a second copy of anything a single accident could destroy.
